India Weather Alert conditions for August 22, 2026 are expected to remain closely watched as the country continues through an active phase of the monsoon season while some regions may also experience uncomfortable heat and humidity. Heavy showers, thunderstorms, waterlogging and localized flooding can remain important concerns across rain-prone parts of India, while areas receiving weaker rainfall may continue to face high daytime temperatures and heat stress. The combination of intense rainfall, warm temperatures and changing weather patterns highlights the growing need for residents to follow local forecasts and official warnings. Weather conditions can change rapidly during the monsoon, making district-level alerts especially important for travel, farming and daily activities.
Heavy rainfall is likely to remain one of the main weather concerns across India as moisture-rich monsoon winds continue to influence several regions. During this period of August, central, western, eastern and northeastern parts of the country can experience spells of moderate to very heavy rain depending on the position of monsoon systems. Strong thunderstorms may also accompany rainfall in some locations, increasing the possibility of temporary power disruption, poor visibility and traffic delays. Urban centres are particularly vulnerable when intense rain falls within a short period because drainage systems can quickly become overwhelmed.
People living near rivers, low-lying neighbourhoods, hills and areas with a history of flooding should pay extra attention to local advisories. Mountainous regions can face additional hazards including landslides, falling rocks and blocked roads after repeated rainfall. Travelers should therefore check weather and road conditions before beginning long journeys. Farmers may benefit from rainfall in agricultural areas, but prolonged or excessive precipitation can damage standing crops, delay field work and increase the risk of soil erosion. The actual severity of rainfall will vary significantly from one state or district to another.
While monsoon rainfall is affecting many areas, rainfall distribution is rarely uniform across the country. Locations experiencing extended breaks between showers can see temperatures rise sharply, particularly when cloud cover decreases. High humidity can make these temperatures feel even more uncomfortable because the human body becomes less efficient at cooling itself through sweating. Such conditions may create heatwave-like stress even where official heatwave criteria are not reached.
Residents should remain cautious during the hottest afternoon hours, especially children, older people, outdoor workers and those involved in physically demanding activities. Drinking sufficient water, wearing lightweight clothing and avoiding unnecessary exposure to direct sunlight can reduce heat-related discomfort. Warm nights may also become a concern in densely populated cities where buildings and roads retain daytime heat. The contrast between heavy rain in one region and intense heat in another demonstrates how varied India’s weather can be during the late monsoon period.
India’s monsoon weather is strongly influenced by low-pressure systems, monsoon trough movement, moisture from surrounding seas and regional atmospheric circulation. Even small shifts in these systems can significantly change where the heaviest rainfall occurs. A district that receives only light rain during the morning may experience intense thunderstorms later in the day, while another location under an earlier warning may receive less rainfall than expected.
This variability makes short-range and nowcast weather information particularly important. Thunderstorms can bring lightning, strong wind gusts and short but intense bursts of rainfall. In cities, commuters may face sudden traffic congestion and waterlogged roads. In rural areas, lightning can be particularly dangerous for people working in open fields. Residents should therefore avoid relying only on broad national forecasts and should check state or district-specific official updates whenever severe weather is possible.
Extreme rainfall, flooding and periods of intense heat are receiving growing attention because climate change can increase the severity of certain weather extremes. A warmer atmosphere can hold more moisture, potentially contributing to intense rainfall events under suitable atmospheric conditions. At the same time, rising temperatures can increase the frequency and intensity of dangerous heat in many regions.
Rapid urban development can further increase these risks. Concrete surfaces reduce natural water absorption, while construction in flood-prone areas can make heavy rainfall more damaging. Cities can also experience the urban heat island effect, where built-up areas remain warmer than surrounding regions. Climate resilience therefore requires stronger drainage infrastructure, better flood management, heat-action planning and reliable early-warning systems. Individual weather events cannot automatically be attributed to climate change, but long-term warming can influence the conditions in which extreme events develop.
People should follow official local warnings because weather conditions may change quickly from one district to another. A few basic precautions can reduce risks during severe rain, thunderstorms or very hot conditions.
- Avoid travelling through flooded or heavily waterlogged roads.
- Stay away from rivers, drains and rapidly flowing water during intense rainfall.
- Avoid standing under isolated trees during thunderstorms and lightning.
- Check local weather alerts before travelling to hill or flood-prone areas.
- Drink enough water and limit prolonged outdoor activity during extreme heat.
- Keep phones charged and emergency supplies available when severe weather is forecast.

Here in the Southeast, temperatures have soared this summer. Extreme heat can be uncomfortable and it can put additional strain on the cardiovascular system. Dr. Noreen Kelly, a cardiologist at Atrium Health Sanger Heart & Vascular Institute, explains how heat can affect your heart health and what you can do to stay safe when temperatures climb.
How the heat can affect your heart
“It’s been consistently shown that heat can increase our risk of heart attack, stroke, heart failure, hospitalization, abnormal heart rhythm and sudden cardiac death,” says Kelly.
When your body gets hot, it works harder to cool itself. Blood vessels widen to help release heat through the skin, which can lower blood pressure. That can be especially significant for people who are already prone to low blood pressure because of an underlying health condition or medications such as blood pressure-lowering drugs or diuretics, she explains.
Sweating and dehydration can also reduce the amount of fluid circulating in the body and disrupt electrolyte levels. In response, the heart may need to beat faster and work harder to maintain blood flow and blood pressure.
“Our heart rate has to go up to maintain our blood pressure,” she says. “As our heart rate goes up, our heart has to work harder. When our heart works harder, that’s more stressful on our heart, especially for people who have an underlying heart condition.” Electrolytes, including sodium and potassium, also play an important role in maintaining a normal heart rhythm.
“We rely heavily on having normal electrolyte levels in our body to maintain a normal heart rhythm,” says Kelly. “When those electrolyte levels get out of whack, we can predispose ourselves to having abnormal heart rhythms.”
Ask your doctor if supplementing with electrolyte drinks or powders is safe for you.
How to protect your heart in extreme heat
When temperatures soar, Kelly recommends spending as much time as possible in air-conditioned spaces. If you do go outside, aim for cooler morning or evening hours, take frequent breaks, seek shade when possible, use a portable fan and drink water before, during and after time in the heat.
If you have heart failure, follow a fluid restriction or take medications that affect blood pressure or fluid balance, ask your healthcare provider how to adjust your hydration plan during extreme heat. Don’t change your medications or fluid intake on your own.
“Exercise is important, so we don’t want people to stop exercising in these extreme temperatures, but want to make sure they know how to do it safely,” she says.
On especially hot days, that may mean shortening an outdoor workout, moving it to a cooler time of day or exercising indoors instead.
Pay attention to your local air quality index
In addition to checking the weather forecast, pay attention to your local Air Quality Index (AQI). Heat can worsen air quality and air pollution can place additional stress on the heart and lungs.
“Poor air quality can make it challenging to breathe, especially if you have an underlying lung condition, which is just another added stress on your body,” says Kelly. “Our heart and lungs work together, so if it’s really hot and the quality isn’t good, it can be especially stressful on the body.”
When to seek medical attention for heat-related illness
Pay attention to how you feel when you’re outside in the heat. Dizziness, headache, nausea, weakness, heavy sweating or shortness of breath can be signs that your body is becoming overheated. Stop what you’re doing, move to a cooler place and let someone know you aren’t feeling well.
If you feel lightheaded or like your heart is racing, Kelly recommends resting in a cool area and contacting your physician if symptoms persist or you’re concerned. Follow your care team’s recommendations for hydration, particularly if you have heart failure or have been told to limit fluids.
Confusion, loss of consciousness, seizures or a very high body temperature can be signs of heat stroke, which is a medical emergency. Call 911 and begin cooling the person while waiting for help.
Older adults and people who have had a heart attack or stroke, have heart failure, or take medications that affect blood pressure or fluid balance may be particularly susceptible to extreme heat.
Finally, Kelly recommends building a relationship with a primary care provider or cardiologist who can help you understand your individual risk factors and make a plan to stay safe during extreme heat.
Learn more about heart care at Atrium Health Sanger Heart & Vascular Institute.

Rajasthan has a yellow alert for rain in 15 districts on Friday, while 13 districts are under a yellow alert for August 22. The Meteorological Department has forecast weak monsoon conditions across the state for four to five days from August 23.
On Thursday, Dholpur recorded the highest rainfall at 29 mm. In Jaipur, JLN Marg received the highest rainfall at 17 mm. Light rain was also reported in parts of Kota, Jhalawar, Bharatpur and Dausa.
With most parts of the state receiving little rain in recent days, temperatures have started rising. Sri Ganganagar remained the hottest place in Rajasthan on Thursday, recording a maximum temperature of 40.1°C.
Big monsoon updates
Dholpur receives more than 1 inch of rain: Light to moderate rain occurred at isolated places in the Bharatpur, Jaipur and Kota divisions of eastern Rajasthan on Thursday. In the last 24 hours, Dholpur recorded the highest rainfall of 29 mm. Basai Nawab in Dholpur received 19 mm, Tehla in Alwar 16 mm, Shahbad in Baran 17 mm, Baran city 16 mm and Tonk 11 mm. Light rain of less than 10 mm was also recorded in Kota, Jhalawar, Bharatpur and Dausa.
Monsoon to remain weak across most areas: Meteorological Department Director Radheshyam Sharma said the well-marked low-pressure system over eastern India has weakened into a low-pressure area. The monsoon trough is currently passing through Amritsar, Nizamabad, Fatehgarh and Hardoi before extending towards the Bay of Bengal through the low-pressure area.
Weather is likely to remain dry across most of the Jodhpur and Bikaner divisions for the next week. However, isolated light rain may occur in Sri Ganganagar, Hanumangarh, Churu and adjoining areas between August 21 and 23. Most parts of the Udaipur, Kota and Ajmer divisions in eastern Rajasthan are also likely to experience weak monsoon conditions for about a week.
Weather in major Rajasthan cities
Jaipur: 17 mm rain on JLN Marg
Jaipur remained partly sunny from morning until afternoon on Thursday. The weather changed after noon as clouds gathered and rain occurred in several parts of the city. Light to moderate rain was reported around JLN Marg, Ajmeri Gate, Rambagh, 22 Godam, Transport Nagar and Malviya Nagar.
JLN Marg recorded 17 mm of rain, while Jaipur Airport received 1.4 mm. The city recorded a maximum temperature of 34.3°C and a minimum of 27°C.
Alwar: Light to heavy rain
The weather changed in Alwar on Thursday after nearly a week. Clouds covered the city in the morning, followed by sunshine in the afternoon. Around 5:30 pm, light to heavy rain lashed parts of the city.
Nearly half an hour of rain caused waterlogging in some areas and brought relief from the heat. The Meteorological Department has forecast thunderstorms and rain between August 21 and 23.
Ajmer: Clouds remain throughout the day
The monsoon has remained weak in Ajmer for several days. Although clouds form over the city daily, the lack of significant rain has increased humidity. Cloudy conditions continued on Thursday. The Meteorological Department has issued a yellow alert for rain on August 21. Ajmer recorded a maximum temperature of 31.1°C and a minimum of 23.8°C.
Kota: Humidity troubles residents
Clouds remained over Kota throughout Thursday, with occasional sunshine. The maximum temperature dropped by 1°C, but residents continued to struggle with heat and humidity. The city recorded a maximum temperature of 32.6°C and a minimum of 26.3°C. The Meteorological Department has issued a two-day rain alert for the Kota division.
Udaipur: Wait for rain continues
Clouds covered Udaipur from Thursday morning, but sunshine prevailed for most of the day. Clouds returned in the evening, but the city did not receive rain. Udaipur recorded a maximum temperature of 30.6°C and a minimum of 23.2°C on Thursday.
Jodhpur: Clouds gather but no rain
Jodhpur experienced normal weather on Thursday, with cloudy conditions throughout the day but no rain. The maximum temperature was 33.9°C, 0.1°C below normal, while the minimum was 26.8°C, 1°C above normal. The Meteorological Department has forecast no rain in the city over the next few days.

Monaco records its longest marine heatwave as sea temperatures stay above 28°C
Monaco is experiencing an unprecedented marine heatwave, with Mediterranean sea temperatures remaining above 28°C for 39 consecutive days.
The record-breaking period began on 14 July.
Listen to this article
Marine biologist Stéphanie Reynaud-Berthier, from the Monaco Scientific Centre, says the duration is unlike anything previously observed at a human timescale.
The prolonged heat is putting increasing pressure on marine wildlife and plant life, including corals.
Scientists warn that while some species can temporarily survive high temperatures by using their energy reserves, these reserves eventually become depleted.
The effects are particularly concerning for red coral, which grows by just 2–3mm a year.
Repeated heatwaves leave little time for damaged colonies to recover.
The heat is also reaching deeper waters.
At around 40 metres, temperatures in Monaco would normally range between 14°C and 18°C, but the unusually long period of warm weather and lack of wind is pushing the warmer water progressively deeper.
Mobile species such as fish can move towards cooler waters, but fixed organisms such as coral have no such escape route.
Scientists say the current episode should not be viewed as an isolated anomaly, but as a sign of a new reality for the Mediterranean - with the key question now being whether marine ecosystems can adapt quickly enough to increasingly frequent and prolonged heatwaves.

Heatwave puts emergency services under pressure across the Riviera
Emergency departments across the Alpes-Maritimes and Var are under mounting pressure after weeks of intense heat.
Hospitals are reporting record patient numbers and emergency services handling thousands of calls every day.

At Nice University Hospital, emergency admissions reached a record 350 patients on 30 July, compared with around 260 to 270 on a normal day.
August has seen an average of about 310 admissions a day.
In both the Alpes-Maritimes and Var, the SAMU is receiving more than 2,000 calls per department each day - a level previously associated mainly with peak summer dates such as Bastille Day and 15 August.
Hospitals in the Var are also struggling with demand.
At Toulon-La Seyne Hospital, the proportion of emergency patients requiring admission has risen from around 20-30% normally to 40-45% this summer.
Fréjus-Saint-Raphaël Hospital briefly activated its Level 2 Plan Blanc after recording more than 260 emergency admissions in a single day.
Older residents are among those worst affected.
At Nice University Hospital, people aged over 75 normally account for around a quarter of emergency patients, but this summer they have represented more than one in three.
Doctors say the prolonged heat is also causing widespread exhaustion and sleep problems, particularly among people with cardiovascular or kidney conditions.
The strain comes as France records a significant increase in heat-related deaths, with around 7,000 excess deaths reported nationally between 17 June and 22 July.

That “chance” appeared to have receded as of Thursday. The Met Office’s long-range forecast, covering the period September 3-17, predicted a “rather unsettled” start to autumn, with all areas “probably seeing a mixture of showers or longer spells rain interspersed with drier interludes.”
It continued: “Temperatures likely varying around average, some warm or hot spells are possible but unlikely prolonged in early September.
“By mid-September, there may be an increase in the extent of drier, more settled weather, especially in the south and east, though signals become very weak.”
However, an update on Friday has once again opened the door to another hot spell over London.
It acknowledges that the weather is going to be “most likely changeable at first” with rain “across many areas, perhaps heavy and thundery in places”.
But an improvement appears to be on the horizon as the month progresses.
It states: “Further into September, drier weather may become more prevalent, especially in the south and southeast, with any more unsettled conditions tending to become confined further north and northwest.
Read More
“Temperatures will probably be near normal at first, but may turn warmer later with a chance of some hot periods in the south.”
The latest forecast comes after a thunderstorm warning for parts of northern England expired on Thursday morning.
The UK is facing increasingly severe weather extremes such as heatwaves, droughts and flooding – with a risk of surface water floods as heavy rain falls on baked dry ground – as a result of climate change, caused mostly by burning fossil fuels for power stations, vehicles, heating buildings and industry.
Nearly three quarters of England including London, and all of Wales, are in drought as a result of the hot and dry conditions.

Garaadka Macmalka ah (AI) ayaa wax ka beddelaya suuqa shaqada: Waa kuwee shaqooyinka khatarta ku jira?
Shirkadaha ku hawlan dhinaca garaadka macmalka ah (AI) ayaa sameeya sheegashooyin waaweyn oo ku saabsan awoodda qalabkooda ay ugu beddeli karaan shaqaalaha aadanaha.
Hawlaha qaarkood si buuxda ayaa loo otomaatig looga digi doonaa, halka kuwa kalena la beddeli doono lana horumarin doono iyadoo la adeegsanayo garaadka macmalka ah.
Madaxda shirkadaha ugu waaweyn dunida ayaa balaayiin doollar ku maalgelinaya teknoolojiyaddan, iyagoo og in adeegsiga qalabkani uu yareyn karo kharashaadka shaqaalaha.
Maalmahan, madaxda shirkadaha waxaa loo sheegayaa in "in la ilaaliyo tirada shaqaalaha oo isku mid ah ay tahay calaamad muujinaysa guul iyo wax-soo-saar," halka maalgashadayaashu ay isweydiinayaan in shaqooyinka loo dhiibo shaqaale cusub iyo in kale, ama loo dhiibo "wakiillo garaadka macmalka" — shaqaale dijitaal ah oo loo kireysto inay qabtaan hawlo gaar ah, kuwaas oo qaarkood xitaa awood u leh inay qabtaan shaqooyin u baahan khibrad gaar ah.
Haddii xitaa kala bar sheegashooyinkan ay run noqdaan, saameyntooda dhammaanteen waan dareemi doonnaa, dhammaan qaybaha dhaqaalaha iyo xirfadaha aan ku shaqaysanno.
Dhaqaalyahanno ku guuleystay abaalmarinta Nobelka ayaa dhawaan ka digay in dunidu ay tahay inay "la qaado tallaabo degdeg ah" si loo hubiyo in garaadka macmalka ahi uu abuuro barwaaqo isla markaana uu hagaajiyo heerka nolosha, halkii uu sababi lahaa in shaqooyin badan la waayo oo ay dad badan shaqo la'aan ku dhacdo.
Bishii hore, ganacsiyada ku yaalla London ayaa ka digay inay ku adag tahay inay helaan xirfadaha ay u baahan yihiin, xilli garaadka macmalka ee dijitaalka ahi uu isbeddello waaweyn ku keenayo suuqa shaqada.
Weli waxaan ku jirnaa marxaladihii hore, balse xogtu waxay durba muujinaysaa isbeddello xiiso leh. Xogtu waxay muujinaysaa sida shabakadaha garaadka macmalka ee kala duwan ay u qaban karaan hawlo ay horey u qaban jireen aadanuhu.
Marka la eego cabbirkan, saddex sano oo keliya ka hor, nidaamyada waaweyn ee luuqadda (LLMs) waxay si hufan u qaban karaan oo keliya hawlo uu qofku ku dhammayn karo dhowr ilbiriqsi ama daqiiqado.
Hadda, nidaamyadani waxay sii kordhinayaan awoodda ay u leeyihiin inay qabtaan hawlo ka adag, kuwaas oo qofka ku qaadan lahaa ku dhowaad hal saac.
Qaar ka mid ah nidaamyada waaweyn ee luuqadda ayaa hadda xitaa awood u leh inay aqoonsadaan dhibaatooyinka ku jira qandaraasyada lacagaha dijitaalka ah, isla markaana ay abuuraan ama horumariyaan nidaamka laftiisa — hawlo qofka ku qaadan lahaa dhowr saacadood inuu dhammaystiro.
shaqooyiinka uu saameyn doono garaadka Macmalka (AI)
Jiilka cusub ee nidaamyadan ayaa la filayaa inuu awood u yeesho inuu inta badan shaqadiisa naqshadaynta iyo horumarinta iskiis u qabto, isaga oo aan ku tiirsanaan taageero adanaha ka timaadda, muddo ku dhow sannadka soo socda.
Isbeddelkan ayaa hadda si weyn uga muuqda dhinaca barnaamijyada iyo horumarinta nidaamyada kombiyuutarrada. Inkasta oo isbeddelkani weli ku jiro marxaladihii hore, haddana waxaa sidoo kale laga arkayaa dhinacyo kale sida falanqaynta maaliyadda, shaqooyinka bilowga ah ee dhinaca sharciga, iyo xitaa qaar ka mid ah shaqooyinka bilowga ah ee warshadaha hal-abuurka.
Daraasadda ugu dhammaystiran ee ilaa hadda la sameeyay waxay ka timid Maraykanka, iyadoo la adeegsanayo xog afar sano ah oo ku saabsan xaaladda shaqo ee kooxo da' oo kala duwan, kuwaas oo ka shaqeeya xirfado heerar kala duwan ugu nugul garaadka macmalka ah (AI).
Shaqooyinkaas waxaa ka mid ah horumarinta barnaamijyada kombiyuutarrada, shaqaalaha xarumaha adeegga macaamiisha, shaqaalaha daryeelka caafimaadka, xannaaneeyayaasha carruurta iyo timo-jareyaasha.
Falanqayn ay samaysay Jaamacadda Stanford oo ku saabsan xogta mushaharka iyo shaqaalaynta ayaa muujinaysa in tan iyo markii ay soo baxeen chatbots, shaqaalaynta dadka da'doodu u dhaxayso 22 ilaa 25 sano ay hoos u dhacday 2.7 boqolkiiba.
Hoos-u-dhacu wuxuu gaarayaa 12.8 boqolkiiba qaybaha sida weyn ay u saameeyeen AI, oo ay ka mid yihiin maaliyadda, horumarinta barnaamijyada iyo ganacsiyada hal-abuurka ku yimid.
Dabcan, dhammaan dhaqaaleyahannadu kuma raacsana gunaanadkan. Qaar waxay aaminsan yihiin in arrimo kale, oo ay ka mid yihiin kororka dulsaarka iyo xaaladda guud ee dhaqaalaha, ay sidoo kale sharxi karaan isbeddelladan ka dhacay suuqa shaqada.
Xayeysiisyada shaqooyinka ee internetka ayaa sidoo kale saameyn ka qaaday ChatGPT iyo nidaamyada kale ee waaweyn ee luuqadda Kombiyuutarka ee loo yaqaanno (LLMs).
Dabcan, waxaa jira arrimo kale oo badan oo xaaladdan ka qayb qaadanaya, laga bilaabo dulsaarka ilaa siyaasadaha canshuuraha.
Si kastaba ha ahaatee, mid ka mid ah natiijooyinka ugu yaabka badan ee ka soo baxay falanqayn dhowaan ay samaysay Ururka Iskaashiga Dhaqaalaha iyo Horumarinta (OECD) ayaa ah farqiga u dhexeeya tirada xayeysiisyada shaqooyinka ee qaybaha sida weyn u saameeyay AI iyo kuwa aan sida weyn u saameyn.
Daraasadda ayaa muujisay in shaqooyinka ay ka mid yihiin suuq-geynta telefoonka iyo adeegyada sharciga ay ka mid yihiin qaybaha sida weyn u saameeyay AI, halka meelaha sida dhismaha, adeegyada nadaafadda iyo diyaarinta cuntada ay ka mid yihiin kuwa ugu yar ee uu saameeyay.
Dalka UK waxaa laga diiwaangeliyay hoos-u-dhac weyn oo ku yimid tilmaamahan, iyadoo dulsaarkuna uu ahaa mid aan isbeddelin ama hoos u dhacay, halka isbeddelkani uu sidoo kale billowday ka hor intii aysan kharashaadku kor u kicin sannadkii hore.
Marka loo eego tilmaamayaal badan oo caalami ah, ku-tiirsanaanta weyn ee dhaqaalaha UK uu ku qabo waaxda adeegyada ayaa dalka ka dhigaysa mid u nugul in shaqooyin la waayo, maadaama uu sii fidayo garaadka macmalka ah.

Isticmaalka AI waxaa lagu cabbiraa halbeeg loo yaqaan "token".
Token-yadu waa qaybo yaryar oo qoraal ah oo nidaamyada AI ay u isticmaalaan inay fahmaan, falanqeeyaan oo soo saaraan luuqad. Celcelis ahaan, token kasta wuxuu u dhigmaa qiyaastii saddex-meelood meel afar meelood meel kelmad Ingiriisi ah.
Shirkadaha ugu waaweyn ee dunida ee ka shaqeeya garaadka macmalka ah (AI) ayaa xitaa sameeyay "liisaska kala sarreynta token-yada" si ay shaqaalahooda ugu dhiirrigeliyaan inay gaaraan heerar wax-soo-saar oo sare, iyagoo adeegsanaya nidaamyada ugu casrisan.
Bilihii u dambeeyay, isticmaalka token-yadu wuxuu gaaray tirilyanno, mararka qaarna wuxuu gaaray tobanaan tirilyan ama xitaa quadrillions, taas oo inta badan ay sabab u tahay adeegsiga "wakiillada AI" — nidaamyo awood u leh inay qabtaan hawlo kala duwan iyaga oo aan faragelin bini'aadan u baahnayn.
Si kastaba ha ahaatee, waxaa jira caqabado. Kharashka isticmaalka teknoolojiyaddan ayaa si weyn u kordhay, ilaa heer ay shirkado badan hadda qasab ku noqotay inay xakameeyaan oo yareeyaan isticmaalka nidaamyadan.
Arrintani waa muhiim, sababtoo ah waxay muujin kartaa inay jiraan xaddidaad ku saabsan awoodda nidaamyada iskii u shaqeeya.
Xaaladaha qaarkood, "adeegsiga dijitaalka ah" ayaa ka qaalisan kara shaqaalaha aadanaha, iyadoo ay ku xiran tahay nooca shaqada la qabanayo.
Si kastaba ha ahaatee, waxaa jira qodob kale oo muhiim ah oo la xuso. Shirkado badan, oo ay ku jiraan kuwa ku yaalla dalalka reer Galbeedka, ayaa bilaabay inay isticmaalaan nidaamyada AI ee kharashka ugu yar, kuwaas oo lagu dhisay teknoolojiyad laga sameeyay Shiinaha, laguna soo bandhigay suuqa lacag la'aan ama qiimo aad u hooseeya.
Sidaas darteed, weli waxaa jira hubanti la'aan badan oo ku saabsan saameynta AI ku yeelan doonto suuqa shaqada, balse isbeddello muuqda ayaa durba soo baxaya.

As we head into the tail end of summer, it might be tempting to throw in the towel and run your home’s air conditioning at full blast after getting home from back-to-school shopping or returning from the farmers market. But those of us who run budget-minded and environmentally conscious households may be looking for other ways to beat the heat. Fortunately, there are plenty of simple tricks that can help keep your home comfortable without running up the electric meter.
When August heat settles in, it’s easy to reach for the air conditioner and leave it running around the clock. But before modern air conditioning became commonplace, people relied on shade, airflow and careful timing to keep their homes comfortable. Many of those techniques still work today.
Whether you’re trying to lower your energy bill, give your air conditioner a break or simply make the house more comfortable during a heat wave, a few small changes can make a noticeable difference.
Keep the Sun Out
One of the easiest ways to prevent a house from overheating is to keep sunlight from coming inside in the first place. Close curtains, blinds or shades on windows that receive direct sunlight, particularly on the south- and west-facing sides of the house.
Exterior shade can be even more effective. Awnings and shutters can help block the sun while also adding some character to your home’s exterior. If you would rather employ nature’s solution, consider planting shade trees in strategic places to block the sun’s rays before they reach your windows. Obviously, this is more of a long-term project, but it can pay dividends in the years to come.
Deciduous trees are a great option because they block the sun during the summer while allowing sunlight through in the autumn and winter after their leaves fall.
Open Windows at the Right Time
Counterintuitively, opening every window during a heat wave isn’t always a good idea. Depending on the time of day, open windows can actually bring more heat into the house than they let out.
If temperatures drop after sunset, open windows on opposite sides of the house to create cross-ventilation. Cool nighttime air can help flush out the heat that accumulated indoors during the day. Close the windows and shades again in the morning before outdoor temperatures begin to climb.
While a bit more tedious than simply adjusting your thermostat, this routine was standard practice before modern air conditioning became ubiquitous. It remains an effective low-tech way to manage indoor temperatures when conditions are favorable.
Put Your Fans to Work
Fans don’t actually lower the temperature of a room, but they can make people feel considerably cooler by increasing air movement across the skin.
Ceiling fans are a great solution in warm weather, pushing air downward and creating a cooling breeze. Just remember to turn them off when you leave the room. Fans cool people, not the room itself.
Box fans and window fans can also be useful alternatives to air conditioning. If the outdoor air is cooler than the air inside, place one fan in a window facing outward to exhaust hot indoor air and another on the opposite side of the house to draw in cooler outdoor air. This works particularly well overnight when outdoor temperatures drop.
Close Off Hot Rooms
Some rooms naturally collect more heat than others. These rooms should be kept closed if possible. Kitchens have a habit of becoming warm after cooking, while upstairs bedrooms tend to heat up as warm air rises. If you have rooms that aren’t being used, keep their doors closed to limit the amount of warm air circulating through the rest of the house.
If your kitchen really puts off a ton of heat, consider firing up the outdoor grill or using a slow cooker to make meals during a heat wave. Depending on the size and layout of your home, avoiding the oven can help keep temperatures down in the rest of the house.
Don’t Add Unnecessary Heat
A variety of household appliances produce enough excess heat to affect your home’s overall temperature, so be mindful of how and when you use them when the mercury is pushing through the roof.
Ovens, dryers, incandescent bulbs and even a computer tower running all day can contribute small amounts of heat to your home. During a heat wave, consider running heat-producing appliances during the cooler morning or evening hours.
Switching to LED bulbs is another easy improvement. LEDs use less energy and produce considerably less waste heat than traditional incandescent bulbs.
Make the Most of Your Basement
Basements tend to be cooler than the rest of the house because they are below ground and surrounded by soil, which tends to stay relatively cool. Many basements are also built primarily from concrete, which can absorb and retain heat.
Warm air rises, while cooler air settles toward the lowest levels of the house. Retreating to the basement rather than immediately turning on the air conditioner can therefore be a time-honored way to stay comfortable during a heat spell.
Keep the Attic From Becoming an Oven
A hot attic can make the rooms below it considerably warmer, so proper attic insulation can help keep the livable spaces in your home cooler. Adequate ventilation also allows hot air trapped in the attic to escape.
Attic vents, soffit vents and ridge vents can work together to keep air moving through the roof space. If your attic routinely becomes extremely hot, improving insulation and ventilation can be well worth the investment.
Sometimes the Old Ways Still Work
Air conditioning is truly a modern wonder, but it hasn’t always been available. For generations, people found clever ways to keep their homes comfortable using shade, airflow and good timing.
You don’t have to give up air conditioning altogether to benefit from these old-fashioned methods. Even simple changes, such as closing the blinds during the hottest part of the day, opening the windows at night or using a fan strategically, can take some of the pressure off your air conditioner and your electric bill.

Chandigarh Tricity remained largely dry on Thursday despite the India Meteorological Department’s (IMD) yellow alert for heavy rain at isolated places, as the weather system that triggered Tuesday’s flashflood-like conditions weakened further.
The dry spell provided respite to civic agencies engaged in restoring roads and public utilities damaged by Tuesday’s intense rainfall, when large parts of the Tricity were inundated. Several roads, bridges and drainage structures were damaged.
With rainfall activity subsiding, temperatures began to rise again in Chandigarh. The maximum temperature climbed to 35.7°C, an increase of 1.3 degrees over Wednesday, while remaining 2.9 degrees above normal. The minimum temperature also rose marginally to 25.4°C, up 2.2 degrees from the previous night, but remained 0.1 degree below normal. The relative humidity remained high, ranging between 67% and 89%.
The IMD has issued no weather warning for Friday, but a yellow alert for Saturday has been retained, with heavy rain at isolated places forecast. There will be no weather warning from Sunday onwards, although rain is likely at isolated places on the following days.
Tuesday’s intense rainfall had significantly narrowed Chandigarh’s seasonal rainfall deficit. The city’s cumulative rainfall since June 1 stood at 550.2 mm till 5.30 pm on Thursday, which was still 13% below normal. The figure marks a substantial improvement from the 26.4% deficit recorded before Tuesday’s intense spell.
